claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The as-cast alloy provides good strength and plasticity but insufficient long-term performance under extreme and variable conditions.
The proposed intervention is aging at approximately 600 °C for 1 hour in argon followed by quenching to room temperature.
Using an argon atmosphere during aging will avoid oxidation.
The aging treatment will form nanoscale intermetallic precipitates within the lamellae or at lamellar interfaces.
The precipitated phase may be B2 or another stable intermetallic phase.
The precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The precipitates will restrict grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and restricted grain-boundary sliding will delay creep onset.
The precipitates will stabilize mechanical performance under cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses.
Aging will increase yield strength relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
Aging will increase creep resistance relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
Aging will maintain or improve ductility relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
The benefits may be sensitive to deviations from the specified aging time or temperature.
The predicted improvements apply at ambient and moderately elevated temperatures and may not extend beyond the designed operating environments.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained, whereas the falsification rule can be read as requiring a statistically significant enhancement in ductility. Under that reading, an outcome explicitly permitted by the prediction would count as falsification.
